newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds, futures pull up to close, remain cautious.
newsitem.headline: Bunds, futures pull up to close, remain cautious.

text.p: German debt prices were heading back towards base in late trade on Wednesday, recovering losses sustained during the day.

Traders said the market was very quiet, but suffering still from the uncertainty over how Germany plans to plug its deficit holes after the government was forecd to back down on plans to take a one-off payment from Bundesbank reserves.
"We had some early weakness on profit-taking but support held up and it wasn't protracted," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
By 1502 GMT, the June DTB Bund futures was trading four basis points higher at 101.51, having spent most of the session languishing between 10 and 15 basis points lower.

In the cash market, traders said volumes were very low but buyers had begun to step in again at lower levels. The 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 101.25 for a 5.825 percent bid yield by 1505 GMT.
A trader in Frankfurt said continued political wrangling over the budget deficit was tainting the trading background.
"That is weighing on the market," he said.
Diebel agreed, saying players were becoming more and more sceptical of the timing of EMU's start, and of its strength.
"The gold issue has receded, and now it is very hard to see how Germany can make up for the shortfall," he said.
"Despite the fact politicians are still protesting that EMU will go ahead on time and the criteria will be met, the mathematics of the whole thing just don't add up."
For Bunds, however, analysts said such concerns were more or less 'business as usual' and would not have any significant immediate impact on the market.
In the short-term, the main focus for Bunds will be German gross domestic product and unemployment data due on Thursday an Friday.
Forecasts are that the German economy grew a mere 0.3 percent in the first quarter, which analysts said is likely to another layer to EMU worries.
The unemployment rate is forecast to have dipped slightly to 11.2 percent in May from 11.3 percent in April.
